producer_report.summary: Added `cargo run -p xtask -- site [--out <dir>]`. It renders the firstmate work-handling study into one self-contained `site/index.html` (inline CSS, viewport meta, responsive grid, dark mode via prefers-color-scheme, no external assets). All text comes from the study JSON and is HTML-escaped. Every state, counter, transition and rationale links to claim ids. The claims are listed with source paths and lines. The pinned commit from pin.json is stated at the top and in the footer. The study's findings are shown under their own finding ids, since they are not claims. An unknown claim id, an element that cites no claim, or a missing or malformed study file is an error. No new dependency was needed, so Cargo.lock is unchanged. `/site` is gitignored. New `.github/workflows/pages.yml` (a governance file) runs on a push to main and on workflow_dispatch. It builds with `cargo run --locked -p xtask -- site` and deploys with configure-pages, upload-pages-artifact and deploy-pages. Permissions are contents read, pages write and id-token write, with a `pages` concurrency group. I also wrote the design note `docs/design/explainer-site.md` (alternatives and deferrals), a CHANGELOG entry, and a README section with the local command, the expected Pages URL and the owner step of setting Pages source to GitHub Actions. policy.rs and docs/non-rust-files.md now list pages.yml in the YAML allow-list. In the requirements map, row D2-1 now points at the new files but stays "Not covered", because the strategy-view coverage counts are test-checked and nothing is live yet. ci.yml, athena.toml, defaults.toml, rust-toolchain.toml and the lint tables are unchanged.

checks_run.note: The whole workspace passed. That includes five new site renderer tests (escaping, claim-id citation and pinned commit, unknown claim id, missing data, output location) and the policy tests.
It exited 0 and wrote site/index.html from the real study. I removed the output afterwards. git status showed no tracked changes from it.

open_issues: The owner must set Settings -> Pages -> Source to GitHub Actions and let the workflow run on main. The live URL (HTTP 200) is not verified; nothing here can check it.

pages.yml pins the three Pages actions by major version tag (configure-pages@v5, upload-pages-artifact@v3, deploy-pages@v4), not by commit SHA as ci.yml does, because I could not look up the SHAs offline. The design note lists pinning them as a deferral. The checkout step uses the same pinned SHA as ci.yml.
The README gives the Pages URL as a template, https://<owner>.github.io/<repository>/, because the repository's owner and name are not in the tree.
The pages.yml build job relies on rust-toolchain.toml and the runner's rustup to install the pinned toolchain. I did not run it on GitHub, only locally.
mistakes: I first ran the full `cargo test` with verbose output, and I could not read the saved output file. I re-ran it with --quiet.
learnings: xtask/tests/policy.rs keeps an allow-list of non-Rust code that must match docs/non-rust-files.md. A .yml file is not flagged by extension, but the allow-list names workflows.

strategy.rs derives requirement status from the cell prefix (Not covered, Partial, Covered). A test compares it with the counts table in strategy-view.md, so changing a row's status needs a matching edit to that table.
Claim text in claims.json starts with a bracketed tag such as [mechanism] or [prose-only]; the renderer shows it as a badge.
The Bash hook only allows listed commands, and Read/Grep refuse paths outside the working directory. That includes the saved tool-output files.
desires: The GitHub owner and repository name, to write the exact Pages URL.
Commit SHAs for the official Pages actions, so they can be pinned.
